text: Let $α,α+2,α\in 𝐙$, be the roots of the quadratic equation $x(x+2)+(x+1)(x+3)+(x+2)(x+4)+\ldots .+(x+\mathrm{n}-1)(x+\mathrm{n}+1)=4\mathrm{n}$ for some $\mathrm{n}\in 𝐍$. Then $\mathrm{n}+α$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The left side is $\sum\limits _{k=0}^{n-1}(x+k)(x+k+2)$, with $(x+k)(x+k+2)=x^{2}+2(k+1)x+k(k+2)$.

$\sum\limits _{k=0}^{n-1}2(k+1)=n(n+1),\sum\limits _{k=0}^{n-1}k(k+2)=\dfrac{(n-1)n(2n-1)}{6}+n(n-1)=\dfrac{n(n-1)(2n+5)}{6}$

So $nx^{2}+n(n+1)x+\dfrac{n(n-1)(2n+5)}{6}=4n$; dividing by $n$ and using $(n-1)(2n+5)-24=2n^{2}+3n-29$:

$x^{2}+(n+1)x+\dfrac{2n^{2}+3n-29}{6}=0$

Sum of roots: $2α+2=-(n+1)\Rightarrow α=-\dfrac{n+3}{2}$ and $α+2=-\dfrac{n-1}{2}$.

Product of roots: $\dfrac{(n+3)(n-1)}{4}=\dfrac{2n^{2}+3n-29}{6}\Rightarrow 3n^{2}+6n-9=4n^{2}+6n-58\Rightarrow n^{2}=49\Rightarrow n=7$.

Then $α=-5$ (the equation is $x^{2}+8x+15=0$ with roots $-5$ and $-3$), and $n+α=7-5=2$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers such that $50\left (\frac{2x}{1+3i}-\frac{y}{1-2i}\right )=31+17i,i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then the value of $10(x-3y)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$50\left (\frac{2x}{1+3i}-\frac{y}{1-2i}\right )=31+17i$

We need to find $10(x-3y)$.

First, simplify the fractions by rationalising the denominators.

$\frac{2x}{1+3i}=\frac{2x(1-3i)}{(1+3i)(1-3i)}$

$=\frac{2x(1-3i)}{1+9}=\frac{2x(1-3i)}{10}$

$=\frac{x}{5}(1-3i)$

Similarly,

$\frac{y}{1-2i}=\frac{y(1+2i)}{(1-2i)(1+2i)}$

$=\frac{y(1+2i)}{1+4}=\frac{y(1+2i)}{5}$

Now substitute into the given equation:

$50\left (\frac{x}{5}(1-3i)-\frac{y}{5}(1+2i)\right )=31+17i$

Take $\frac{1}{5}$ common inside:

$50\cdot \frac{1}{5}[x(1-3i)-y(1+2i)]=31+17i$

$10[x(1-3i)-y(1+2i)]=31+17i$

Expand:

$10[x-3xi-y-2yi]=31+17i$

$10[(x-y)+(-3x-2y)i]=31+17i$

So,

$10(x-y)+10(-3x-2y)i=31+17i$

Now compare real and imaginary parts:

$10(x-y)=31$

$10(-3x-2y)=17$

Thus,

$x-y=\frac{31}{10}$

$-3x-2y=\frac{17}{10}$

Now solve these equations.

From the first equation,

$x=y+\frac{31}{10}$

Substitute into the second:

$-3\left (y+\frac{31}{10}\right )-2y=\frac{17}{10}$

$-3y-\frac{93}{10}-2y=\frac{17}{10}$

$-5y=\frac{17}{10}+\frac{93}{10}$

$-5y=\frac{110}{10}=11$

$y=-\frac{11}{5}$

Then

$x=y+\frac{31}{10}=-\frac{11}{5}+\frac{31}{10}$

$x=-\frac{22}{10}+\frac{31}{10}=\frac{9}{10}$

Now find:

$10(x-3y)=10\left (\frac{9}{10}-3\left (-\frac{11}{5}\right )\right )$

$=10\left (\frac{9}{10}+\frac{33}{5}\right )$

$=10\left (\frac{9}{10}+\frac{66}{10}\right )$

$=10\cdot \frac{75}{10}=75$

Therefore, the value of $10(x-3y)$ is

$75$

So, the correct option is $\text{D}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Let $α,β\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ be such that the system of linear equations

$\begin{array}{ll} x+2y+z & =5 \\ 2x+y+αz & =5 \\ 8x+4y+βz & =18 \end{array}$

has no solution. Then $\frac{β}{α}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} x+2y+z=5 \\ 2x+y+αz=5 \\ 8x+4y+βz=18 \end{array}$

For a system of three linear equations to have no solution, it is necessary that the coefficient matrix be singular, i.e. its determinant is zero: $\Delta =0$.

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & α \\ 8 & 4 & β \end{array}\right |=0 \\ \Delta =1(β-4α)-2(2β-8α)+1(0)=0 \\ =β-4α-4β+16α=0 \\ \Rightarrow 4α=β \end{array}$

Now substitute $β=4α$ in the third equation. Then the left side of the third equation becomes $8x+4y+4αz$, which is exactly $4$ times the left side of the second equation $2x+y+αz$.

But the constants do not match: $4\times 5=20$, whereas the third equation has $18$. So we get $4\times (2x+y+αz)=20$ but $8x+4y+4αz=18$, which is a contradiction. Hence, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

Therefore, $\dfrac{β}{α}=\dfrac{4α}{α}=4$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

solution.body:

trace of matrix

text: Let A be the set of first 101 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 1 and the common difference is 5 and let B be the set of first 71 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 9 and the common difference is 7. Then the number of elements in $A\cap B$, which are divisible by 3, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Understand Set A

Set $A$ consists of the first 101 terms of an A.P. with the first term $a=1$ and common difference $d_{1}=5$. 

The $n$-th term of this A.P. is given by the formula:

$a_{n}=a+(n-1)d_{1}$

Therefore, the last term (101st term) of Set A is:

$a_{101}=1+(101-1)\times 5=1+100\times 5=501$

So, $A=\{1,6,11,16,21,\ldots ,501\}$.

Understand Set B

Set $B$ consists of the first 71 terms of an A.P. with the first term $b=9$ and common difference $d_{2}=7$.

The $m$-th term of this A.P. is:

$b_{m}=b+(m-1)d_{2}$

Therefore, the last term (71st term) of Set B is:

$b_{71}=9+(71-1)\times 7=9+70\times 7=499$

So, $B=\{9,16,23,30,\ldots ,499\}$.

Find the elements in $A\cap B$

The elements common to both sets $A$ and $B$ will themselves form an A.P. 

From the initial terms listed above, we can easily see that the first common term is $16$.

The common difference of this new A.P. will be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the common differences of the two original sets:

$\text{Common difference of}A\cap B=\text{LCM}(5,7)=35$

The $k$-th term of the common sequence is given by:

$C_{k}=16+(k-1)35$

Since a common term must exist in both sets, it cannot be greater than the smallest of their last terms. Thus, $C_{k}\leq \text{\min }(501,499)$.

$16+(k-1)35\leq 499$

$35(k-1)\leq 483$

$k-1\leq \frac{483}{35}$

$k-1\leq 13.8$

Since $k$ must be a positive integer, the maximum possible value for $(k-1)$ is $13$. Thus, $k\leq 14$. 

There are altogether 14 common terms in $A\cap B$. 

Find elements in $A\cap B$ divisible by 3

We want to find terms $C_{k}$ that are divisible by $3$, which means:

$C_{k}\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}3)$

$16+35(k-1)\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}3)$

Since $16=3\times 5+1⟹16\equiv 1(\mathrm{mod}3)$ and $35=3\times 11+2⟹35\equiv 2(\mathrm{mod}3)$, we can simplify:

$1+2(k-1)\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}3)$

Checking the first few integer values for $k$:

If $k=1$: $1+2(0)=1$ (Not divisible by 3)

If $k=2$: $1+2(1)=3\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}3)$ (Divisible by 3)

If $k=3$: $1+2(2)=5\equiv 2(\mathrm{mod}3)$ (Not divisible by 3)

The condition holds true when $k=2$. Because we are operating in modulo $3$, the values of $k$ that satisfy this condition will form an A.P. with a common difference of $3$. 

Thus, the valid values of $k$ within the range $1\leq k\leq 14$ are:

$k\in \{2,5,8,11,14\}$

Counting these, there are exactly $5$ valid values of $k$.

For confirmation, the terms are: 

For $k=2\to 51$

For $k=5\to 156$

For $k=8\to 261$

For $k=11\to 366$

For $k=14\to 471$

All 5 of these terms are common elements between the sets and are completely divisible by 3.

Correct Answer:

Option B
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: The number of seven-digit numbers, that can be formed by using the digits 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 such that each digit is used at least once, is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each of the five digits $1,2,3,5,7$ appears at least once in the 7 places, so the 2 extra places hold either one digit used twice more or two different digits used once more each.

Pattern $3,1,1,1,1$: the digit used three times is chosen in ${}^{5}C_{1}=5$ ways and the 7 digits are arranged in $\dfrac{7!}{3!}=840$ ways, giving $5\times 840=4200$ numbers.

Pattern $2,2,1,1,1$: the two digits used twice are chosen in ${}^{5}C_{2}=10$ ways and the 7 digits are arranged in $\dfrac{7!}{2!2!}=1260$ ways, giving $10\times 1260=12600$ numbers.

No digit is 0, so every arrangement is a seven-digit number:

$4200+12600=16800$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: The number of elements in the set $S=\left \{(r,k):k\in \mathrm{ℤ}\text{and}^{36}C_{r+1}=\frac{6\left ({}^{35}C_{r}\right )}{(k^{2}-3)}\right \}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We need to find the number of ordered pairs $(r,k)$ satisfying

${}^{36}C_{r+1}=\frac{6\left ({}^{35}C_{r}\right )}{k^{2}-3},$

where $k\in \mathrm{ℤ}$.

Let us simplify the relation using the standard NCERT combination formula.

We know that

${}^{n}C_{r+1}=\frac{n!}{(r+1)!(n-r-1)!}$

and

${}^{n-1}C_{r}=\frac{(n-1)!}{r!(n-r-1)!}.$

So,

$\frac{{}^{36}C_{r+1}}{{}^{35}C_{r}}=\dfrac{\dfrac{36!}{(r+1)!(35-r)!}}{\dfrac{35!}{r!(35-r)!}}=\frac{36!}{35!}\cdot \frac{r!}{(r+1)!}=36\cdot \frac{1}{r+1}=\frac{36}{r+1}.$

Hence,

${}^{36}C_{r+1}={}^{35}C_{r}\cdot \frac{36}{r+1}.$

Given,

${}^{36}C_{r+1}=\frac{6\left ({}^{35}C_{r}\right )}{k^{2}-3}.$

Comparing both expressions,

${}^{35}C_{r}\cdot \frac{36}{r+1}=\frac{6\left ({}^{35}C_{r}\right )}{k^{2}-3}.$

Since ${}^{35}C_{r}\neq 0$, cancel it:

$\frac{36}{r+1}=\frac{6}{k^{2}-3}.$

Cross-multiplying,

$36(k^{2}-3)=6(r+1).$

Divide by $6$:

$6(k^{2}-3)=r+1.$

So,

$r=6k^{2}-19.$

Now $r$ must be valid for the combinations ${}^{35}C_{r}$ and ${}^{36}C_{r+1}$.

Thus,

$0\leq r\leq 35.$

Substitute $r=6k^{2}-19$:

$0\leq 6k^{2}-19\leq 35.$

Add $19$ throughout:

$19\leq 6k^{2}\leq 54.$

Divide by $6$:

$\frac{19}{6}\leq k^{2}\leq 9.$

Now possible integer square values are

$k^{2}=4\text{or}k^{2}=9.$

So the integer values of $k$ are:

If $k^{2}=4$, then $k=\pm 2$

If $k^{2}=9$, then $k=\pm 3$

Now find corresponding $r$:

For $k^{2}=4$,

$r=6(4)-19=24-19=5.$

So pairs are

$(5,2),(5,-2).$

For $k^{2}=9$,

$r=6(9)-19=54-19=35.$

So pairs are

$(35,3),(35,-3).$

Hence total number of elements in the set $S$ is

$4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is:

$4$

So, Option B is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
If the mean of the data
Class5-1010-1515-2020-2525-3030-35Frequency2k2854k + 15is 21, then $k$ is one of the roots of the equation:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the grouped data, we first find the class marks of each class interval.

The classes are:

$5-10,10-15,15-20,20-25,25-30,30-35$

So their class marks are:

$7.5,12.5,17.5,22.5,27.5,32.5$

The frequencies are:

$2,k,\qquad 28,54,k+1,5$

Now use the formula for mean of grouped data:

$\bar{x}=\frac{\sum f_{i}x_{i}}{\sum f_{i}}$

Given mean $=21$.

Now calculate $\sum f_{i}$:

$\sum f_{i}=2+k+28+54+(k+1)+5$

$\sum f_{i}=2k+90$

Now calculate $\sum f_{i}x_{i}$:

$\sum f_{i}x_{i}=2(7.5)+k(12.5)+28(17.5)+54(22.5)+(k+1)(27.5)+5(32.5)$

Now simplify step by step:

$2(7.5)=15$

$28(17.5)=490$

$54(22.5)=1215$

$5(32.5)=162.5$

$(k+1)(27.5)=27.5k+27.5$

So,

$\sum f_{i}x_{i}=15+12.5k+490+1215+27.5k+27.5+162.5$

$\sum f_{i}x_{i}=40k+1910$

Now apply the mean formula:

$21=\frac{40k+1910}{2k+90}$

Cross-multiply:

$21(2k+90)=40k+1910$

$42k+1890=40k+1910$

$2k=20$

$k=10$

Now we check which equation has $k=10$ as a root.

Option A:

$2x^{2}-23x-10=0$

Put $x=10$:

$2(10)^{2}-23(10)-10=200-230-10=-40\neq 0$

Option B:

$4x^{2}-35x+24=0$

Put $x=10$:

$4(10)^{2}-35(10)+24=400-350+24=74\neq 0$

Option C:

$2x^{2}-19x-10=0$

Put $x=10$:

$2(10)^{2}-19(10)-10=200-190-10=0$

So $10$ is a root.

Hence, the correct option is:

$\text{Option C}2x^{2}-19x-10=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Let the mid points of the sides of a triangle ABC be $\left (\frac{5}{2},7\right )$, $\left (\frac{5}{2},3\right )$ and $(4,5)$. If its incentre is $(h,k)$, then $3h+k$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let the midpoints of the sides of triangle $ABC$ be

$D\left (\frac{5}{2},7\right ),E\left (\frac{5}{2},3\right ),F(4,5)$

We have to find the incentre $(h,k)$ of triangle $ABC$.

Step 1: Use the fact about the medial triangle
The triangle formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle is called the medial triangle.

If the midpoints are known, then the original triangle can be reconstructed using:

$A=E+F-D,B=F+D-E,C=D+E-F$

Now calculate each vertex.

Vertex $A$
$A=\left (\frac{5}{2},3\right )+(4,5)-\left (\frac{5}{2},7\right )$

$A=(4,1)$

Vertex $B$
$B=(4,5)+\left (\frac{5}{2},7\right )-\left (\frac{5}{2},3\right )$

$B=(4,9)$

Vertex $C$
$C=\left (\frac{5}{2},7\right )+\left (\frac{5}{2},3\right )-(4,5)$

$C=(1,5)$

So the triangle has vertices

$A(4,1),B(4,9),C(1,5)$

Step 2: Find the side lengths
Using distance formula:

Side opposite $A$, i.e. $BC$
$BC=\sqrt{(4-1)^{2}+(9-5)^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$

Side opposite $B$, i.e. $CA$
$CA=\sqrt{(4-1)^{2}+(1-5)^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+(-4)^{2}}=5$

Side opposite $C$, i.e. $AB$
$AB=\sqrt{(4-4)^{2}+(9-1)^{2}}=8$

Thus,

$a=5,b=5,c=8$

Step 3: Use incentre formula
The incentre of triangle with vertices $A(x_{1},y_{1})$, $B(x_{2},y_{2})$, $C(x_{3},y_{3})$ is

$\left (\frac{ax_{1}+bx_{2}+cx_{3}}{a+b+c},\frac{ay_{1}+by_{2}+cy_{3}}{a+b+c}\right )$

where

$a=BC$

$b=CA$

$c=AB$

Substitute the values:

$h=\frac{5\cdot 4+5\cdot 4+8\cdot 1}{5+5+8}=\frac{20+20+8}{18}=\frac{48}{18}=\frac{8}{3}$

$k=\frac{5\cdot 1+5\cdot 9+8\cdot 5}{18}=\frac{5+45+40}{18}=\frac{90}{18}=5$

So the incentre is

$\left (\frac{8}{3},5\right )$

Step 4: Find $3h+k$
$3h+k=3\cdot \frac{8}{3}+5=8+5=13$

Therefore, the answer is

$13$

So, the correct option is Option C.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Let an ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $a<b$, pass through the point (4, 3) and have eccentricity $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$.
Then the length of its latus rectum is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $a<b$, the major axis is along the $y$-axis. So for the ellipse

$\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1,$

we use the eccentricity formula

$e=\sqrt{1-\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}}.$

Given

$e=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3},$

so

$e^{2}=\frac{5}{9}.$

Hence,

$1-\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}=\frac{5}{9}$

which gives

$\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}=1-\frac{5}{9}=\frac{4}{9}.$

Therefore,

$a^{2}=\frac{4}{9}b^{2}.$

Now the ellipse passes through $(4,3)$, so it satisfies the equation:

$\frac{4^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{3^{2}}{b^{2}}=1.$

That is,

$\frac{16}{a^{2}}+\frac{9}{b^{2}}=1.$

Substitute $a^{2}=\frac{4}{9}b^{2}$:

$\frac{16}{\frac{4}{9}b^{2}}+\frac{9}{b^{2}}=1.$

Simplifying,

$16\cdot \frac{9}{4b^{2}}+\frac{9}{b^{2}}=1$

$\frac{36}{b^{2}}+\frac{9}{b^{2}}=1$

$\frac{45}{b^{2}}=1$

so

$b^{2}=45.$

Then

$a^{2}=\frac{4}{9}\cdot 45=20.$

For an ellipse with major axis along the $y$-axis, the length of latus rectum is

$\frac{2a^{2}}{b}.$

So,

$\text{Length of latus rectum}=\frac{2\cdot 20}{\sqrt{45}}=\frac{40}{3\sqrt{5}}.$

Rationalising,

$\frac{40}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{8\sqrt{5}}{3}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is

$\dfrac{8\sqrt{5}}{3}$

So, Option D is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: If $\sin \left (\frac{π}{18}\right )\sin \left (\frac{5π}{18}\right )\sin \left (\frac{7π}{18}\right )=K$, then the value of $\sin \left (\frac{10Kπ}{3}\right )$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let

$K=\sin \left (\frac{π}{18}\right )\sin \left (\frac{5π}{18}\right )\sin \left (\frac{7π}{18}\right )$

We need to find

$\sin \left (\frac{10Kπ}{3}\right )$

First, write the angles in degrees:

$\frac{π}{18}=10^{\circ },\frac{5π}{18}=50^{\circ },\frac{7π}{18}=70^{\circ }$

So,

$K=\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 50^{\circ }\sin 70^{\circ }$

Now use the standard identity:

$\sin 3x=4\sin x\sin (60^{\circ }+x)\sin (60^{\circ }-x)$

Taking $x=10^{\circ }$,

$\sin 30^{\circ }=4\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 70^{\circ }\sin 50^{\circ }$

Since

$\sin 30^{\circ }=\frac{1}{2}$

we get

$\frac{1}{2}=4\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 50^{\circ }\sin 70^{\circ }$

Hence,

$\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 50^{\circ }\sin 70^{\circ }=\frac{1}{8}$

Therefore,

$K=\frac{1}{8}$

Now substitute in the required expression:

$\sin \left (\frac{10Kπ}{3}\right )=\sin \left (\frac{10}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{8}π\right )=\sin \left (\frac{10π}{24}\right )=\sin \left (\frac{5π}{12}\right )$

Now,

$\frac{5π}{12}=75^{\circ }$

So,

$\sin 75^{\circ }=\sin (45^{\circ }+30^{\circ })$

Using the formula $\sin (A+B)$:

$\sin 75^{\circ }=\sin 45^{\circ }\cos 30^{\circ }+\cos 45^{\circ }\sin 30^{\circ }$

$=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{2}$

$=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}$

So the value is

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Hence, the correct option is A.

text: Let $S=\{x\in [-π,π]:\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=a,a\in \mathrm{ℤ}\}$. Then $n(S)$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We need to find the number of elements in

$S=\{x\in [-π,π]:\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=a,a\in \mathrm{ℤ}\}.$

So we must find all $x\in [-π,π]$ for which the value

$\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)$

is an integer.

Step 1: Simplify the expression
Let

$f(x)=\sin x(\sin x+\cos x).$

Then

$f(x)=\sin ^{2}x+\sin x\cos x.$

Now use the identities:

$\sin ^{2}x=\frac{1-\cos 2x}{2},\sin x\cos x=\frac{\sin 2x}{2}.$

So,

$f(x)=\frac{1-\cos 2x}{2}+\frac{\sin 2x}{2}=\frac{1+\sin 2x-\cos 2x}{2}.$

Also,

$\sin 2x-\cos 2x=\sqrt{2}\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right ).$

Hence,

$f(x)=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )}{2}.$

Step 2: Find the range of $f(x)$
Since

$-1\leq \sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )\leq 1,$

we get

$-\sqrt{2}\leq \sqrt{2}\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )\leq \sqrt{2}.$

Therefore,

$\frac{1-\sqrt{2}}{2}\leq f(x)\leq \frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}.$

Now,

$\frac{1-\sqrt{2}}{2}\approx -0.207,\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}\approx 1.207.$

So the only integers possible in this interval are

$0~\text{and}1.$

Thus we need to solve:

$f(x)=0$

$f(x)=1$

Step 3: Solve $f(x)=0$
We have

$\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=0.$

So either

Case 1:
$\sin x=0$

In $[-π,π]$, this gives

$x=-π,0,π.$

Case 2:
$\sin x+\cos x=0$

That is,

$\sqrt{2}\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )=0$

so

$x+\frac{π}{4}=nπ\Rightarrow x=nπ-\frac{π}{4}.$

Now check in $[-π,π]$:

for $n=0$, $x=-\frac{π}{4}$

for $n=1$, $x=\frac{3π}{4}$

other values go outside the interval

So from $f(x)=0$, we get

$x=-π,0,π,-\frac{π}{4},\frac{3π}{4}.$

Total $5$ values.

Step 4: Solve $f(x)=1$
We need

$\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=1.$

Using the simplified form:

$\frac{1+\sqrt{2}\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )}{2}=1.$

So,

$1+\sqrt{2}\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )=2$

$\sqrt{2}\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )=1$

$\sin \left (2x-\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.$

Now,

$\sin θ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

when

$θ=\frac{π}{4}+2nπ\text{or}θ=\frac{3π}{4}+2nπ.$

So,

First possibility:
$2x-\frac{π}{4}=\frac{π}{4}+2nπ$

$2x=\frac{π}{2}+2nπ$

$x=\frac{π}{4}+nπ$

In $[-π,π]$, this gives

$x=\frac{π}{4},-\frac{3π}{4}.$

Second possibility:
$2x-\frac{π}{4}=\frac{3π}{4}+2nπ$

$2x=π+2nπ$

$x=\frac{π}{2}+nπ$

In $[-π,π]$, this gives

$x=\frac{π}{2},-\frac{π}{2}.$

So from $f(x)=1$, we get $4$ values:

$x=\frac{π}{4},-\frac{3π}{4},\frac{π}{2},-\frac{π}{2}.$

Step 5: Total number of elements
Combining both cases:

from $a=0$: $5$ values

from $a=1$: $4$ values

Hence,

$n(S)=5+4=9.$

So the correct answer is:

$9$

Therefore, Option D is correct.

text: If the point of intersection of the lines $\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y+a}{5}=\frac{z+b+1}{7}$ and $\frac{x-2}{1}=\frac{y-b}{4}=\frac{z-2a}{7}$  lies on xy-plane, then the value of $a+b$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the common point of intersection of the two lines be $P$.

Since the point lies on the $xy$-plane, its $z$-coordinate must be $0$.

We write both lines in parametric form.

For the first line,

$\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y+a}{5}=\frac{z+b+1}{7}=λ$

So,

$x=3λ-1,y=5λ-a,z=7λ-b-1$

For the second line,

$\frac{x-2}{1}=\frac{y-b}{4}=\frac{z-2a}{7}=μ$

So,

$x=μ+2,y=4μ+b,z=7μ+2a$

At the point of intersection, coordinates are equal.

So we get:

$3λ-1=μ+2$

$5λ-a=4μ+b$

$7λ-b-1=7μ+2a$

Also, since the point lies on the $xy$-plane,

$z=0$

Hence from both lines:

$7λ-b-1=0$

and

$7μ+2a=0$

Now solve step by step.

From

$3λ-1=μ+2$

we get

$3λ-μ=3\Rightarrow μ=3λ-3$

From $z=0$ in the first line,

$b=7λ-1$

From $z=0$ in the second line,

$2a=-7μ\Rightarrow a=-\frac{7μ}{2}$

Now use

$5λ-a=4μ+b$

Substitute $μ=3λ-3$, $b=7λ-1$:

$5λ-a=4(3λ-3)+(7λ-1)$

$5λ-a=12λ-12+7λ-1$

$5λ-a=19λ-13$

$-a=14λ-13$

$a=13-14λ$

Also,

$a=-\frac{7μ}{2}=-\frac{7(3λ-3)}{2}$

$a=\frac{-21λ+21}{2}$

Equate the two values of $a$:

$13-14λ=\frac{-21λ+21}{2}$

Multiply by $2$:

$26-28λ=-21λ+21$

$5=7λ$

$λ=\frac{5}{7}$

Then

$μ=3λ-3=3\cdot \frac{5}{7}-3=\frac{15}{7}-\frac{21}{7}=-\frac{6}{7}$

Now find $a$ and $b$.

$b=7λ-1=5-1=4$

$a=-\frac{7μ}{2}=-\frac{7}{2}\left (-\frac{6}{7}\right )=3$

Therefore,

$a+b=3+4=7$

So the correct answer is:

$7$

Option C

text: Let a line L passing through the point (1, 1, 1) be perpendicular to both the vectors $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. If $P(a,b,c)$ is the foot of perpendicular from the origin on the line L, then the value of $34(a+b+c)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Direction vector of line is

$=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \end{array}\right |=-2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$


[IMG]


So equation of line is

$\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-1}{-3}=\frac{z-1}{2}=λ\text{let}$

let ( $2λ+1,-3λ+1,2λ+1$ ) be the foot of perpendicular from $(0,0,0)$ upon given line

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \mathrm{OM}\leftarrow \cdot (2\hat{\mathrm{i}}-3\mathrm{j}+2\hat{\mathrm{k}})=0 \\ \Rightarrow 2(2λ+1)-3(-3λ+1)+2(2λ+1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow λ=-\dfrac{1}{17} \end{array}$

So $(\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c})\equiv \left (\frac{-2}{17}+1,\frac{3}{17}+1,\frac{-2}{17}+1\right )$

$\Rightarrow 34(a+b+c)=100$

solution.body:
$\therefore$ Denominator $=0$ at $x=2$

$\Rightarrow$ Numerator $=0$ at $x=2$

text: If the curve $y=f(x)$ passes through the point $(1,e)$ and satisfies the differential equation $dy=y(2+\log _{e}x)dx$, $x>0$, then $f(e)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=y(2+\ln x)$

To solve this, first separate the variables by dividing both sides by $y$:

$\int \frac{dy}{y}=\int (2+\ln x)dx$

Now integrate both sides. The left side gives $\ln y$. For the right side, integrate term by term:

$\ln y=2x+x\ln x-x+C$

Combine like terms $2x-x=x$:

$\ln y=x+x\ln x+C$

Since it passes through $(1,e)$, put $x=1$ and $y=e$ in the equation. Then $\ln y=\ln e=1$ and $\ln 1=0$:

$1=1+0+C\to C=0$

So the required relation becomes:

$\ln y=x+x\ln x$

Taking antilog (exponential) on both sides:

$f(x)=y=e^{x+x\ln x}$

Now substitute $x=e$. Also, $\ln e=1$:

$\Rightarrow f(e)=e^{e+e}=e^{2e}$

text:
The number of critical points of the function 

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} |\frac{\sin x}{x}|, & x\neq 0 \\ 1, & x=0 \end{array} \right.$ in the interval $(-2π,2π)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\left |\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right |=1=f(0)$, so $f$ is continuous on $(-2π,2π)$. Its critical points are where $f^{'}(x)=0$ or $f^{'}(x)$ does not exist.

Let $g(x)=\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$ for $x\neq 0$ and $g(0)=1$. Near $x=0$, $g>0$, so $f=g=1-\dfrac{x^{2}}{6}+\ldots$, which gives $f^{'}(0)=0$: $x=0$ is a critical point.

For $x\neq 0$ with $\sin x\neq 0$, $f=\pm g$ near $x$, and

$g^{'}(x)=\dfrac{x\cos x-\sin x}{x^{2}}=0⟺\tan x=x$

since $\cos x=0$ would force $\sin x=0$.

In $(0,2π)$: on $\left (0,\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$, $\tan x>x$; on $\left (\dfrac{π}{2},π\right ]$ and $\left (\dfrac{3π}{2},2π\right )$, $\tan x\leq 0<x$; on $\left (π,\dfrac{3π}{2}\right )$, $\tan x-x$ is increasing (its derivative is $\tan ^{2}x$) from $-π$ to $+\infty$, so there is exactly one root. As $\tan x-x$ is odd, there is exactly one root in $(-2π,0)$, lying in $\left (-\dfrac{3π}{2},-π\right )$. This gives 2 critical points.

At $x=\pm π$, $g(\pm π)=0$ and $g^{'}(\pm π)=\mp \dfrac{1}{π}\neq 0$, so $g$ changes sign there and $f=|g|$ has unequal left and right derivatives $\pm \dfrac{1}{π}$: $f^{'}(\pm π)$ does not exist, giving 2 more critical points.

The critical points are $x=0$, one root of $\tan x=x$ in each of $\left (π,\dfrac{3π}{2}\right )$ and $\left (-\dfrac{3π}{2},-π\right )$, and $x=\pm π$: 5 in all.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation
 $(1+\sin x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+(y+1)\cos x=0,y(0)=0.$ If the curve $y=y(x)$ passes through the point $\left (α,\dfrac{-1}{2}\right )$,
 then a value of $α$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int \frac{dy}{y+1}=-\int \frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}dx$

On the left side, $\int \frac{dy}{y+1}=\ln (y+1)$.

On the right side, take $1+\sin x$ as substitution: let $u=1+\sin x$, then $du=\cos xdx$. So, $-\int \frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}dx=-\int \frac{du}{u}=-\ln (1+\sin x).$

So we get $\Rightarrow \ln (y+1)=-\ln (1+\sin x)+C$

Now use the initial condition $y(0)=0$. Put $x=0$ and $y=0$ in the equation:

$\therefore y(0)=0\to \ln (0+1)=-\ln (1+\sin 0)+C$

That is $0=-\ln (1)+C\Rightarrow C=0.$

So $\Rightarrow \ln (y+1)=-\ln (1+\sin x)$

Taking antilog on both sides, $\Rightarrow y+1=\frac{1}{1+\sin x}$

Given that the curve passes through $\left (α,-\frac{1}{2}\right )$, substitute $y=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=α$:

$-\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{1}{1+\sin α}$

So $\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{1+\sin α}\Rightarrow 1+\sin α=2\Rightarrow \sin α=1$

Now $\sin α=1$ gives $\Rightarrow α=\frac{π}{2}\text{(as per options)}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

solution.body:
For domain $\log _{0.6}\left |\frac{2x-5}{x^{2}-4}\right |\geq 0$

$\left |\frac{2x-5}{x^{2}-4}\right |\leq 1&x\neq \frac{5}{2}\ldots ..(1)$

$-1\leq \frac{2x-5}{x^{2}-4}\leq 1$

$\frac{2x-5}{x^{2}-4}+1\geq 0$

$\frac{x^{2}+2x-9}{x^{2}-4}\geq 0$

$\frac{(x+1)^{2}-10}{(x-2)(x+2)}\geq 0$


[IMG]

$x\in \left (-\infty ,-1-\sqrt{10}\right ]\cup (-2,2)\cup \left [-1+\sqrt{10},\infty \right )\ldots ..(2)$

$\frac{2x-5}{x^{2}-4}-1\leq 0$

$\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{(x-2)(x+2)}\geq 0$

$x\in (-\infty ,-2)\cup (2,\infty )\cup \{1\}\ldots ..(3)$

$(1)\cap (2)\cap (3)$

$x\in \left (-\infty ,-1-\sqrt{10}\right ]\cup \{1\}\cup \left [-1+\sqrt{10},\frac{5}{2}\right )\cup \left (\frac{5}{2},\infty \right )$

$a+b+c+d+e=-2+1+5=4$

text: If $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}a_{k}=6n^{3}$, then $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}\left (\frac{a_{k+1}-a_{k}}{36}\right )^{2}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots +a_{n}=6n^{3}.$ 

To get a formula for one term, write the sum up to $n+1$ terms:

$a_{1}+a_{2}+\cdots +a_{n}+a_{n+1}=6(n+1)^{3}$

Now subtract the first equation from this to isolate $a_{n+1}$:

$a_{n+1}=6(n+1)^{3}-6n^{3}$

Use the identity $x^{3}-y^{3}=(x-y)(x^{2}+xy+y^{2})$ with $x=n+1$ and $y=n$:

$=6((n+1)-n)\left ((n+1)^{2}+n^{2}+n(n+1)\right )$

Since $(n+1)-n=1$, simplify the bracket:

$a_{n+1}=6(1)(3n^{2}+3n+1)$

So, replacing $n$ by $n-1$ gives a formula for $a_{n}$:

$a_{n}=6\left (3(n-1)^{2}+3(n-1)+1\right )$

Now simplify inside:

$=6\left (3(n^{2}-2n+1+n-1)+1\right )$

Combine terms:

$=6(3(n^{2}-n)+1)$

So we get:

$a_{n}=6(3n^{2}-3n+1)$

Now compute $a_{k+1}-a_{k}$ using the formulas:

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}\left (\frac{6(3k^{2}+3k+1)-6(3k^{2}-3k+1)}{36}\right )^{2}$

Inside the bracket, cancel common parts:

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}\left (\frac{36k}{36}\right )^{2}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}k^{2}=\frac{6\times 7\times 13}{6}=91$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Let a, b, c ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}. If the probability, that $ax^{2}+2\sqrt{2}bx+c>0$ for all $x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, is $\frac{m}{n}$, $\gcd (m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the quadratic expression

$ax^{2}+2\sqrt{2}bx+c$

to be positive for all $x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, we use the NCERT condition for a quadratic $Ax^{2}+Bx+C$ to satisfy

$Ax^{2}+Bx+C>0\text{for all}x\in \mathrm{ℝ},$

which is:

$A>0$

Discriminant $<0$

Here,

$A=a,B=2\sqrt{2}b,C=c$

Since $a\in \{1,2,3,4\}$, we always have

$a>0$

So we only need

$D=B^{2}-4AC<0$

Now,

$D=(2\sqrt{2}b)^{2}-4ac=8b^{2}-4ac$

Thus,

$8b^{2}-4ac<0$

Dividing by $4$:

$2b^{2}-ac<0$

So the required condition is

$ac>2b^{2}$

Now $a,b,c\in \{1,2,3,4\}$, so total number of choices is

$4\times 4\times 4=64$

We count favourable triples $(a,b,c)$.

Case 1: $b=1$
Then

$ac>2$

Now $a,c\in \{1,2,3,4\}$. Total pairs $(a,c)$ are $16$.

We exclude pairs with $ac\leq 2$:

$(1,1)$ gives $ac=1$

$(1,2)$ gives $ac=2$

$(2,1)$ gives $ac=2$

So favourable pairs:

$16-3=13$

Case 2: $b=2$
Then

$ac>8$

Possible products greater than $8$ are obtained from:

$(3,3)$ gives $9$

$(3,4)$ gives $12$

$(4,3)$ gives $12$

$(4,4)$ gives $16$

So favourable pairs = $4$.

Case 3: $b=3$
Then

$ac>18$

But maximum possible value of $ac$ is

$4\cdot 4=16$

So no favourable pair.

Case 4: $b=4$
Then

$ac>32$

Again impossible, since maximum $ac=16$.

So no favourable pair.

Hence total favourable triples are

$13+4+0+0=17$

Therefore, the required probability is

$\frac{17}{64}$

Thus,

$m=17,n=64$

and

$m+n=17+64=81$

So the answer is

$81$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: If $α=\int\limits _{0}^{2\sqrt{3}}\log _{2}(x^{2}+4)dx+\int\limits _{2}^{4}\sqrt{2^{x}-4}dx$, then $α^{2}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x)=\log _{2}(x^{2}+4)$ on $[0,\quad 2\sqrt{3}]$. It is increasing there, with $f(0)=\log _{2}4=2$ and $f(2\sqrt{3})=\log _{2}16=4$.

From $y=\log _{2}(x^{2}+4)$, $x^{2}=2^{y}-4$, so $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{2^{x}-4}$ for $x\in [2,4]$. The second integral is therefore $\int\limits _{f(0)}^{f(2\sqrt{3})}f^{-1}(x)dx$.

For an increasing function,

$\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx+\int\limits _{f(a)}^{f(b)}f^{-1}(x)dx=bf(b)-af(a)$
